documentedDuplicates.meta-llama: Slot 3 (llama-3.3-70b-instruct, post-Gemini-demote 2026-05-16) + Slot 9 (llama-4-maverick). Different generations, different serving paths on OpenRouter, independent in practice. Documented per W5b dispatch #2 (2026-05-16, commit 556a751 triggering evidence).

allObjections.title: §1 honest-gate underspecified
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §1 requires refusing to manufacture work, yet the proposal treats a pre-run "honest assessment" as a single-function add (J6 option 2) without defining the substantial-transformation bar, prediction inputs, or false-positive/negative handling. Evidence in §F shows a 99.5 → 85 RelTwin regression, proving current gating is absent; the fix needs calibrated criteria and rollback path, not a minimal patch.

allObjections.title: §6 tool selection not auditable
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §6 mandates per-step top-5 ranking selection and runtime emission of tool.selection envelopes; §F shows 0 such envelopes, and §G shows attachToolIntelligenceService() has 0 call sites. The J6 "single correct" action wires UI→construction but leaves §6 non-conformance intact, risking unaudited executions that continue to violate the Tool Intelligence Principle.

allObjections.title: §2 no-silent-omission patch risky
allObjections.detail: The proposal suggests extending orchestration_complete with dimensions_contributing[] and adding a jurisdiction column to product_registry. §2 requires per-run disclosure and jurisdiction-aware evaluation with auditable amendments; a static registry column may not capture per-environment/per-run jurisdiction declarations, and altering a hot envelope risks bloat and migration errors without a backfill plan for prior entries.

allObjections.title: §5 self-application blocked by flags
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §5 binds FlowAI to apply itself to its own codebase, yet §E shows product_registry.flowai.construction_eligible=false and §F shows 4 self-runs with empty payloads. Enabling construction for FlowAI may also trip CA-17 S2 scope caps (15 files/1500 lines) without a module-level plan; the proposal does not address this conflict.

allObjections.title: §7 Output Contract atomicity gap
allObjections.detail: §7 requires atomic ProductSSOT delta_log writes with output; §F shows delta_log=0 across all rows and §F/G note orchestration_complete payloads often empty. Preview URLs are produced, but without delta_log history, runs should roll back per §10 Self-Protect; the persisted state violates the atomic contract and risks audit drift.

allObjections.title: PATH B data hygiene concerns
allObjections.detail: §E/§G indicate PATH B synthesizes product_ssot rows (e.g., flowai-upgraded-…-ad6c5c54) without product_registry entries. This can orphan governance state and bypass jurisdiction declaration per §2, contravening the "no default jurisdiction" invariant while polluting SSOT with undeclared products.

allObjections.title: Incomplete Tool Intelligence Integration
allObjections.detail: Section §6 mandates runtime emission of tool selection envelopes, but the current implementation does not invoke the Tool Intelligence Service, resulting in zero tool.selection envelopes across all runs. This is a critical gap in the auditability and transparency of the tool selection process.

allObjections.title: Lack of Pre-Run Honest Assessment
allObjections.detail: Section §1 requires FlowAI to refuse to start a run against a product that already meets or exceeds the quality standard. However, the system allowed a run on RelTwin that regressed from a score of 99.5 to 85, indicating a failure to implement this honest assessment gate.

allObjections.title: Silent Omission of Quality Dimensions
allObjections.detail: Section §2 requires that all 10 quality dimensions be optimized and reported on each run. Currently, 6 out of 10 dimensions are silently omitted, and there is no jurisdiction column in the product registry, violating the no-silent-omission rule.

allObjections.title: No Tool Selection Emission

allObjections.title: §1: No pre-run honest gate

allObjections.title: §2: Silent dimension omission
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §2 requires all 10 quality dimensions to be assessed, but the current implementation silently omits 6 dimensions (jurisdiction, accessibility, privacy, legal, syntax, duplication, CSRF). This violates the 'no silent omission' invariant and skews the composite score, providing an incomplete picture of product quality.

allObjections.title: §6: Tool Intelligence un-wired
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §6 mandates per-step tool selection and runtime emission of `tool.selection` envelopes, but the ToolIntelligenceService is not wired into the production runner. This means that the engine is not dynamically selecting tools based on performance, cost, speed, and reliability, and the audit trail is incomplete.

allObjections.title: §1: UI loop incomplete
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §1 promises a URL-in/URL-out loop through the UI, but the current UI only supports auditing and does not trigger the construction engine. This means that users cannot use the UI to create new, deployed URLs, violating the core promise of FlowAI.

allObjections.title: §5: Self-application failure
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §5 states that FlowAI applies to its own development process, but the four self-application runs have empty payloads, and construction against FlowAI itself is gated off. This indicates a failure to fully apply FlowAI's quality standards to its own codebase.

allObjections.title: §1: No trajectory reporting
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §1 requires trajectory reporting after each run, but this feature is not implemented. This makes it difficult for users to track the progress of their runs and make informed decisions about iteration depth.

allObjections.title: §1: No PRs shipped
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §1 promises a new deployable URL, but zero PRs have been shipped across 18 runs. This indicates a fundamental failure to deliver on the core promise of FlowAI.

allObjections.title: §1 Honest Assessment Violation
allObjections.detail: The RelTwin run from 99.5 to 85 score demonstrates FlowAI initiating runs without honest pre-assessment. CA-18 §1 mandates refusing runs when no substantial improvement is possible, yet the engine started against a near-perfect product.

allObjections.title: §2 Silent Dimension Omission
allObjections.detail: Six quality dimensions (accessibility, privacy, legal, syntax, duplication, CSRF) are omitted without findings, violating §2's 'no silent omission' rule. The jurisdiction column absence prevents privacy/legal scoring, yet no findings surface this gap.

allObjections.title: §6 Runtime Disconnect
allObjections.detail: ToolIntelligenceService exists but isn't wired to renewal/orchestrator.js, resulting in 0 tool.selection emissions across 18 runs. This breaches §6's audit contract requiring per-step platform selection visibility.

allObjections.title: Self-Application Blocked
allObjections.detail: product_registry marks FlowAI as construction_eligible=false, blocking §5 self-application. The four self-runs produced empty payloads, violating the symbiotic loop where FlowAI must improve itself.

allObjections.title: No closed URL-out loop
allObjections.detail: In §1 and the J5/J7 evidence, the system can initiate runs and emit preview URLs, but the production UI at `flowai-dun.vercel.app/flowai` does not complete a true input → new deployable URL output path. The proposal itself says PATH B is audit-only in the UI and that no UI affordance triggers construction, which means the core promise remains unfulfilled at the user-facing surface.

allObjections.title: Silent metric omissions remain
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §2 explicitly requires all 10 dimensions to be optimized and mandates that missing dimensions be surfaced as findings rather than skipped. The verifiable state says 6 of 10 dimensions are silently omitted, there is no jurisdiction column, and no `tool.selection` envelopes are emitted; that makes the scoring/reporting layer materially non-compliant, not just incomplete.

allObjections.title: Self-runs are manufactured work
allObjections.detail: §1’s honest-assessment clause forbids starting runs when a product already meets the bar or further iteration is unlikely to produce substantial improvement. The RelTwin example (99.5 → 85 with `exitReason: NO_IMPROVEMENT`) demonstrates the engine launched a run that degraded a high-scoring product instead of refusing upfront, so the current behavior violates the integrity rule the proposal claims is canonical.

allObjections.title: No PRs shipped in 18 runs
allObjections.detail: The proposal claims FlowAI produces a new deployable URL per run, but evidence shows 0 PRs shipped across 18 orchestration_complete entries, indicating a gap between the promise and actual functionality.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the UI is wired to trigger construction (J6 option 3) before adding the §1 honest-assessment gate and §6 tool-selection telemetry, operators can launch construction on already-passing products, induce regressions like 99.5→85, and produce unaudited changes with no ProductSSOT delta_log, degrading trust and compliance versus the current audit-only state.
adversarial.precedent: Microsoft Windows 10 October 2018 Update (version 1809) shipped without adequate pre-release gating and caused data loss regressions — a cautionary example of automated rollout lacking robust guardrails.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: Deferring is prudent: CA-18 §1/§2/§6 have material gaps (no honest gate, silent omissions, missing tool-selection audit), and §7 atomicity is not enforced (delta_log=0). Shipping the URL-in/URL-out surface without these foundations risks regressions and non-compliant runs that cannot be audited or rolled back. Require tool-intelligence wiring, no-silent-omission telemetry, calibrated honest-gate, and SSOT atomic writes before exposing construction through the UI.

J5.pick_text: FAIL — material non-conformance on multiple §1 sub-requirements. Evidence: 0/18 runs shipped a PR (prUrl null everywhere); the most recent RelTwin run regressed -14.5 from 99.5 to 85; 6 of 10 §2 dimensions silently omitted (jurisdiction column absent; accessibility/privacy/legal/syntax/dup/CSRF not measured pipeline-wide); 0 tool.selection envelopes across 18 runs while CA-18 §6 mandates per-step selection emission; 4 FlowAI self-runs have empty payloads; the production UI cannot complete a full URL-in -> new-URL-out cycle. The state matches "engine library partially works" not "FlowAI as defined by CA-18 §1".
J5.rationale: The evidence lists multiple blocking failures across §1/§2/§6 and the UI loop is incomplete; this exceeds a mere "partial" status.

J6.pick_text: Wire the UI submit-URL form to the existing construction engine end-to-end. Concretely: the UI route that accepts any URL must (1) register the URL into product_registry with construction_eligible=true, (2) trigger §29 Build/Wire S1-S8 + §11 Six-Step Clearance via runOrchestration, (3) stream progress + final new URL back to the UI. NO new engine, NO new architecture; this is wiring CA-17 to the existing UI per CA-18 §1 + §5. Single PR scope.
J6.rationale: This is the only listed action that directly closes the URL-in → new-URL-out loop in the product surface, which is the bottleneck to honoring §1 through the UI.

J7.pick_text: MAJOR GAP. UI accepts URLs but does NOT produce a new deployed URL (PATH B is audit-only in the UI; the orchestration runs that DO produce previewUrls are CLI-only). §3 modes are exposed in the UI per code (LandingPage / Configuration / FlowAIDashboard) but no UI affordance triggers construction. §6 top-5-per-step rankings exist in DB (40 rows) but are not surfaced in any GUIDED-mode picker. The UI is consistent with "preview of FlowAI" rather than "FlowAI as CA-18 defines it".
J7.rationale: The UI cannot complete the construction loop and does not surface tool selection; it functions as an audit preview, not the product defined by CA-18.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The next action should be paired with minimal telemetry fixes (tool.selection emission and no-silent-omission arrays) to avoid baking in unaudited behavior, even if not in the same PR.

questions.topic: J5 — Based ONLY on the SSOT documents (CA-18 §1-§6) and the verifiable governance_record + product_registry state below, is the actual codebase + database state consistent with what CA-18 §1 requires FlowAI to produce ("any URL in -> NEW deployable URL out, perfected across 10 quality dimensions per run, with honest assessment + trajectory + diminishing-returns reporting")? PASS at engine layer; FAIL at product layer. The CA-17 §29 Build/Wire engine + §10 Self-Audit + §11 Six-Step Clearance all exist and run; the UI surface that exposes them as a product to operators (CA-18 §1 calls for URL-in/URL-out through the published surface) does not yet close the loop. PASS — CA-18 §1 does not specify the UI as the binding surface; the §1 contract is satisfied by ANY working invocation path that produces input -> new URL. The CLI runs against RelTwin (which produced preview URLs even when finalScore regressed) demonstrate the §1 loop end-to-end. Gaps in §2 + §6 are separate sections, not §1 failures.

questions.topic: J6 — Given the verifiable state below, what is the SINGLE correct next action (ONE action only) that moves FlowAI closest to the CA-18 §1 promise (URL in -> NEW URL out) through its own UI? The Panel must pick ONE action — the others may be valuable but the Panel must rank ONE highest.

options.text: Wire the UI submit-URL form to the existing construction engine end-to-end. Concretely: the UI route that accepts any URL must (1) register the URL into product_registry with construction_eligible=true, (2) trigger §29 Build/Wire S1-S8 + §11 Six-Step Clearance via runOrchestration, (3) stream progress + final new URL back to the UI. NO new engine, NO new architecture; this is wiring CA-17 to the existing UI per CA-18 §1 + §5. Single PR scope.

Wire ToolIntelligenceService into renewal/orchestrator.js by calling attachToolIntelligenceService() at runner init + dispatching step work through OrchestratorHub.invokeStepOwner(). This closes the §6 conformance gap (0 tool.selection envelopes today across 18 runs). Without this, every other §1 claim is unaudited per §6.

Add the §1 pre-run honest-assessment gate that refuses to start a run against an already-passing product (score >= bar OR diminishing-returns predicted). Without this gate, the engine manufactures work (the 99.5 -> 85 RelTwin regression is the canonical example) — a direct §1 violation. The gate is single-function scope.

Extend the self_renewal.orchestration_complete.v1 envelope with dimensions_contributing[] + dimensions_skipped_with_reason[] arrays AND add jurisdiction column to product_registry. This is the minimum change that brings the §2 no-silent-omission invariant into compliance (6 of 10 dimensions are silently omitted today). Wider §2 measurement work follows.

questions.topic: J7 — Based on what CA-18 describes as the product (URL-in/URL-out through its own UI, with §3 AUTOMATIC/GUIDED/MANUAL exposure + §6 tool intelligence visible), is the current production UI at flowai-dun.vercel.app/flowai consistent with that description? Pick the verdict that best fits.

options.text: MAJOR GAP. UI accepts URLs but does NOT produce a new deployed URL (PATH B is audit-only in the UI; the orchestration runs that DO produce previewUrls are CLI-only). §3 modes are exposed in the UI per code (LandingPage / Configuration / FlowAIDashboard) but no UI affordance triggers construction. §6 top-5-per-step rankings exist in DB (40 rows) but are not surfaced in any GUIDED-mode picker. The UI is consistent with "preview of FlowAI" rather than "FlowAI as CA-18 defines it".

PARTIAL GAP — UI structurally aligns with CA-18 (§3 modes visible; URL input accepted; runs can be initiated) but the URL-in -> URL-out closing loop is missing. Add 1-2 wiring fixes and the UI matches the spec.

The UI is fine; the LABELING is the gap. The UI works as an "audit + onboarding" surface today; labeling it "FlowAI" creates the consistency gap with CA-18 §1. Either rename the surface (e.g. "FlowAI Audit") OR wire the construction loop. Cheapest fix: relabel.

CONSISTENT — CA-18 §1 does not bind to a specific URL surface; flowai-dun.vercel.app/flowai is one surface among possible product surfaces. The CLI is another. As long as ONE surface honors §1, CA-18 is satisfied. The UI is a demo / onboarding affordance, not the binding product surface.
